fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: Adder bg3.exe+0x1BA07E0 (8-byte frame storage) defaults it to 0xFFFFFFFF; its only caller bg3.exe+0x1B9F130 then stores *param_1 (a 4-byte key of the surface instance group being created, from bg3.exe+0x1B9B000). Read by ecl::SurfaceManager::Update / RefreshDirtyMaterials (macOS, Toolkit EoCClient.dll+0xAD0670; query Spec<SurfaceInstanceGroupTagComponent, ls::InstancingGroupComponent>). Live: 10 different hash-like values (0x0EEAF7A6..0xA8FC15FD). Windows width: bg3.exe+0x1B9F130 line '*tag = *param_1' is a 4-byte store; param_1 is the instance-group record that its caller bg3.exe+0x1B9B000 looks up by the 4-byte key *(uint*)(param_3+4) (bg3.exe+0x1B9FF60), so +0 is that record's first dword (most likely its own key).

fields.name: field_4
fields.evidence: Adder defaults it to 0xFF; bg3.exe+0x1B9F130 stores the byte at +0xB0 of an object it works on (surface/layer descriptor, not identified). Live 0x0F in all 10 samples - possibly a surface layer/type index. Windows width: bg3.exe+0x1B9F130 '*(byte*)(tag+4) = *(byte*)(param_3+0xB0)' - a 1-byte store from the descriptor passed by the caller as *(param_1+0x70); the adder writes only this byte (0xFF), so +5..+7 stay uninitialised (live: varying garbage).

fields.name: _Pad5
fields.evidence: padding to 8: never written (the adder sets only +0..+4); live bytes vary (uninitialised).

open_questions: Meanings: the 32-bit value at +0 (hash-like key of the surface instance group) and the byte at +4 (copied from +0xB0 of the surface descriptor; 0x0F, 0x0C, 0x30, 0x31 seen).
second_pass: Widths confirmed on Windows: the adder bg3.exe+0x1BA07E0 defaults a 4-byte and a 1-byte member, and the writer bg3.exe+0x1B9F130 stores exactly 4 bytes at +0 and 1 byte at +4; the rest is uninitialised padding. Meanings stay open.
